note: Re-read RFC 8210 Section 8.3, 'When a router receives this, the router SHOULD attempt to connect to any more-preferred caches in its cache list.', together with Section 6, 'The router SHOULD NOT retry sooner than indicated by this parameter.' TestRTRCacheResetReturnsToPreferredCache changed under a ze-test-judge approval: the old round 2 re-asked a cache that had just failed, which Section 6 rules out and poll now refuses. Rounds now: (1) the preferred cache loads and announces a 2s Retry Interval; (2) it answers its Serial Query with No Data Available, and the standby loads by Reset Query, replacing the preferred set (held states checked); (3) the standby answers Serial Query with Cache Reset, the preferred cache is inside its Retry Interval and receives no query, the standby receives the 8.3 Reset Query, the held set is retained, and poll's returned delay must be at most 2s, so the attempt on the more-preferred cache is scheduled for the first moment Section 6 allows; (4) the next round sends the preferred cache a Reset Query, a partial preferred load does not replace the held set, and after End of Data the old-only prefix is NotFound, the shared prefix rejects the old origin and accepts the new, the new-only prefix is Valid, with no further standby query. Starting rounds at the holder, or returning the standby's Refresh or Retry Interval after the Cache Reset, fails the test. Positive (preferred Reset Query and its set used) and negative (standby authorization not retained, standby not queried) are distinct assertions. Revert records on poll re-recorded.
